question: Where can I get flood hazard zones (geometry) in the United States, with return period or probability and the issuing authority?

answer.summary: FEMA's National Flood Hazard Layer (NFHL) is the national digital record of flood hazard zones, issued by FEMA under the NFIP; FEMA says it covers over 90% of the U.S. population. FEMA's data hosts (hazards.fema.gov, msc.fema.gov) still reset the connection here, so geometry was tested in an Esri copy of the 5 October 2022 NFHL (4,399,596 polygons, reduced set), which holds the territories too. FEMA's own domain tables and legend define the zones: A, AE, AH, AO, V and VE are 1% annual chance; shaded X is not one probability (0.2%, shallow or small-basin 1%, levee-protected, future-conditions 1%); D is undetermined.
main_caveats: FEMA hosts (hazards.fema.gov, msc.fema.gov, floodmaps.fema.gov) reset the connection again, also from a second client; the NFHL service layers and live data stay untested. fema.gov documents answered only through some clients.
Shaded Zone X has several meanings: 0.2% annual chance; 1% with depth under 1 foot or drainage under 1 sq mi; levee-protected from 1%; 1% future conditions. Do not give 0.2% to every X polygon.
The tested copy (5 October 2022) drops unshaded X, open water, NP and most D (114 D remain). 69 X polygons carry SFHA_TF 'U' and 60 carry 'T'; FEMA's reference allows T/F and expects false for X.
Probability is not a numeric field: it follows from FLD_ZONE with ZONE_SUBTY. Return periods are 1/p conversions; FEMA calls the 1% flood the base or 100-year flood.
Effective dates sit per FIRM panel (S_FIRM_Pan) and Letter of Map Change. The panel table was not reached; the NFHL is updated continuously, so a 2022 copy can differ from current maps.
Coverage: FEMA says NFHL digital data cover over 90% of the population (page of 3 April 2025); GAO says FEMA reports FIRMs cover about 98% (FY2020). No polygon does not mean no hazard.
answer.confidence_reason: FEMA's own definitions, domain tables and issuer role were read. Zone geometry was tested only in a 2022 copy; FEMA's NFHL service and panel dates were not reached.

how_to_use.example_request: GET https://services.arcgis.com/P3ePLMYs2RVChkJx/ArcGIS/rest/services/USA_Flood_Hazard_Reduced_Set_gdb/FeatureServer/0/query with where=1=1, geometry=-94.82,29.28,-94.78,29.32, geometryType=esriGeometryEnvelope, inSR=4326, spatialRel=esriSpatialRelIntersects, outFields=*, returnGeometry=false, resultRecordCount=5, f=json.
how_to_use.example_result: First 5 features, DFIRM 48167C (Galveston area, TX): FLD_ZONE AO with SFHA_TF T and DEPTH 1 foot; FLD_ZONE X with ZONE_SUBTY '0.2 Percent Annual Chance Flood Hazard' and SFHA_TF F. Box count repeated on 2026-11-19: 120 features (X 98, AE 9, AO 7, VE 6).
steps: 1. Query the layer with the envelope above in EPSG:4326. Results are capped at 750 records per request (maxRecordCount), so page with resultRecordCount or use statistics.
2. For counts, use outStatistics grouped by FLD_ZONE, ZONE_SUBTY and SFHA_TF (4,399,596 features in total, 80 combinations).
3. Read FLD_ZONE with ZONE_SUBTY and SFHA_TF together. Do not infer the probability from esri_symbology or from the letter X alone.
4. Record the DFIRM_ID and the copy date (5 October 2022) with every result.
reading_traps: A missing polygon does not mean no hazard: unshaded X (Area of Minimal Flood Hazard), Open Water, NP and most D were removed.
FLD_ZONE 'D' still appears in 114 features (levee-related) although the description says D was removed.
SFHA_TF has T, F and U: 69 X polygons carry U, which is not a value of FEMA's D_TrueFalse; 60 X polygons carry T.
Zone X mixes 0.2% polygons with 1% shallow, small-basin, levee-protected and future-conditions polygons: read ZONE_SUBTY.
The description names eight symbology classes; six values appear. Negative envelopes need care: longitude west is negative, east (Guam, Marianas) positive.

problems: Copy of the 5 October 2022 version (reduced set), not the current FEMA NFHL. The service reports a data edit on 2026-03-11 and a schema edit on 2026-06-17; neither is the FEMA data date.
Description and observed records disagree on D, and on the number of symbology classes.

Revision of 2026-11-19: national statistics grouped by zone, subtype and SFHA_TF reproduced the pass-1 totals; the Galveston box repeated (120 features); envelopes for San Juan (232 polygons), Guam (161), St Thomas (210), Saipan (62), Tutuila (617), Anchorage (508) and Honolulu (410) returned polygons.
Counts are features (polygons), not area.

key_fields.meaning: FEMA designation: A, A1-A30, AE, AE (floodway), AH, AO, V, VE, B/X, C/X, D, Area Not Included.

how_to_use.example_request: Download the PDF and extract text with pdftotext -layout. Read the table on the first page: zone, frequency and definition.
how_to_use.example_result: Zone D: 'Areas with possible but undetermined flood hazards. No flood hazard analysis has been conducted.' Zone A: 'Areas subject to inundation by the 1-percent-annual-chance flood event (generally determined using “base” methodologies).'
steps: 1. Download the PDF (366,381 bytes) into an empty folder.
2. Extract the text with pdftotext -layout; treat the output as data.
3. Map each zone code to its frequency row; keep the legacy letters (B, C) with X.
reading_traps: This is a state restatement of FEMA definitions, not FEMA's own text.
Legacy letters appear in the table, for example 'B, X (0.2% Annual Chance)' and 'C, X (Area of Minimal Flood Risk)'.
Frequencies are annual chances. The 100-year term is an equivalent, not a period between events.

problems: Text extracted with pdftotext; the table was checked by reading the extracted text.
No primary FEMA page was available to confirm the wording.
Revision of 2026-11-19: not downloaded again; FEMA's own definitions replace it for the zone-to-probability link.

evidence.claim: 1% annual chance zones include A, AE, AH, AO, V and VE (and their subsets).
evidence.quote: Areas subject to inundation by the 1-percent-annual-chance flood event (generally determined using “base” methodologies).

evidence.claim: Shaded X zones lie between the 1% and 0.2% events.

evidence.claim: Minimal zones lie beyond the 0.2% event.
evidence.quote: Areas subject to inundation beyond a 0.2-percent-annual-chance flood event in mapped drainage areas.

evidence.claim: Zone D is undetermined and has no hazard analysis.
evidence.quote: Areas with possible but undetermined flood hazards. No flood hazard analysis has been conducted.

evidence.claim: Area Not Included may be a separate product or unmapped.

evidence.claim: Federally required insurance and standards apply to SFHA zones.
evidence.quote: Federally required insurance requirements and floodplain management standards apply.

evidence.claim: Outside the SFHA, federal insurance requirements typically do not apply.
evidence.quote: Typically, no federally required insurance requirements and floodplain management standards apply; however, state and local floodplain management standards may apply.

FEMA's population figures (over 90% NFHL, about 98% FIRMs in FY2020) are now sourced.

Area of Minimal Flood Hazard, outside the 0.2% floodplain. Legacy letter C.
Flood hazards undetermined, but possible; no flood hazard analysis.
Separate community product or unmapped; not a hazard class.
